A consensus five-star [[college recruit|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class, he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. Duren was selected with the 13th overall pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. On [[NBA draft|draft day]], his rights were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] and subsequently to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He was named an [[NBA All-Star]] and made his first [[All-NBA Team]] selection in the [[2025–26 NBA season]]. ==Early life== Duren was born in [[Sharon Hill, Pennsylvania]], before his family moved to [[New Castle, Delaware]].{{cite news|url=https://www.wdel.com/news/new-castle-resident-taken-in-first-round-of-nba-draft/article_347fb42e-f3a5-11ec-88de-834ab281156f.html|title=New Castle resident taken in first round of NBA Draft|first=Sean|last=Greene|publisher=[[WDEL (AM)|WDEL]]|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=January 30, 2024}} He grew up playing football and baseball in addition to basketball, which he ended up focusing on as he grew older and improved his skills.{{cite news|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/21/getting-know-five-star-roman-catholic-sophomore-center-jalen-duren/2702148001/|title=Getting to know five-star Roman Catholic sophomore center Jalen Duren|work=[[The News-Press]]|first=Alex|last=Martin|date=December 21, 2019|access-date=January 30, 2024}} Duren attended Gunning Bedford Middle School in New Castle, where he played on the basketball team and began attracting attention as a {{Height|ft=6|in=5}} seventh-grader in 2017.{{cite news|url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/2022/06/24/new-castle-resident-taken-first-round-nba-draft/7722754001/|title=Delaware native selected in first round of 2022 NBA draft|first=Kevin|last=Tresolini|work=[[The News Journal]]|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=January 30, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/nba-draft-2022-jalen-duren-roman-catholic-team-final-memphis-20220623.html|title=‘This kid is special’: Jalen Duren’s NBA potential was on display in Philly long before draft night|first=Sam|last=Cohn|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=January 30, 2024}} He was spotted by Rob Brown, the program director for a [[Philadelphia]]-based [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) club called Team Final, who quickly recruited him to the program. By the eighth grade Duren had grown to about {{Height|ft=6|in=8}}, and further grew his profile by leading the 15U Team Final squad to a MADE Hoops League Championship title.{{cite news|url=https://www.madehoops.com/news_article/show/945393|title=MADE Hoops Alumni Series: The Rise Of Jalen Duren Began With The Winter Circuit|work=MADE Hoops|first=Eric|last=Hampford|date=August 30, 2018|access-date=January 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108035751/https://www.madehoops.com/news_article/show/945393|archive-date=January 8, 2021|url-status=dead}} Strong showings at the MADE Hoops Middle School Academy and the CP3 Rising Stars Camp that summer solidified his position as one of the top players in his class.{{cite news|url=https://www.philadelphiasportsdigest.com/news_article/show/991381|title=Boys' Basketball: Jalen Duren Stands Tall as Roman Handles La Salle to Take First Place in Philadelphia Catholic League|work=Philadelphia Sports Digest|first=Rich|last=Flanagan|date=February 3, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}} ==High school career== Duren committed to playing high school basketball at [[Roman Catholic High School]] in Philadelphia, along with AAU teammate and highly ranked guard Justice Williams, after having been personally recruited by head coach Matt Griffin. He averaged 12.8 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 9.3 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 2.5 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game while shooting 71 percent from the field as a freshman, leading his team to their second consecutive [[Philadelphia Catholic League]] title.{{cite news|url=https://phillysportsnetwork.com/2020/12/14/jalen-duren/|title=The recruitment of Philadelphia basketball phenom Jalen Duren|work=Philly Sports Network|first=Leader|last=Johnson|date=December 14, 2020|access-date=January 5, 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://catholicphilly.com/2019/03/news/sports/roman-catholic-takes-2nd-straight-cl-crown-4th-in-5-years/|title=Roman Catholic takes 2nd straight CL crown, 4th in 5 years|work=Catholic Philly|first=John|last=Knebels|date=March 1, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2021}} He earned first-team all-league and second-team all-state honors, and was named a [[MaxPreps]] Freshman All-American.{{cite news|url=https://aopathletics.org/news/2019/5/14/xx-2019-pa-sportswriters-boys-basketball-all-state-team.aspx?path=mbball|title=11 AOP Standouts Named To 2019 PA Sportswriters Team|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=April 19, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2020}} That summer he was a standout performer at the 2019 Nike Elite 100 Camp.{{cite news|url=https://247sports.com/ContentGallery/Emoni-Bates-Michigan-State-Chris-Livingston-Kentucky-Ohio-State-Jalen-Duren-Villanova-Jalen-Washington-Indiana-Purdue-133269470/#133269470_2|title=Nike an 18–10 record.{{cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/high-school-sports/pennsylvania/jalen-duren-roman-catholic-montverde-transfer-20200414.html|title=Roman Catholic star Jalen Duren transfers to Team|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=April 1, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} In the first round of the Catholic League playoffs he recorded 18 points and 18 rebounds against [[Bonner & Prendergast Catholic High School|Bonner-Prendergast]], hitting the game-winning [[buzzer beater]] in the 61–59 victory on [[Valentine's Day]].{{cite news|url=https://www.delcotimes.com/sports/roman-big-man-durens-buzzer-beating-putback-quiets-bonner-prendie/article_932e3de8-4fa5-11ea-ba67-730add6bd3e7.html|title=Roman big man Duren's news|url=https://www.theintell.com/sports/20200219/roman-catholic-big-man-jalen-duren-too-tall-task-for-archbishop-wood|title=Roman Catholic, big man Jalen Duren too tall a task for Archbishop 16 rebounds in the 66–58 loss.{{cite news|url=https://rawsports.tv/wp/coatesville-falls-short-in-attempt-to-knock-off-roman-catholic-in-opening-round-of-6a-state-playoffs-by-tyler-harden/|title=Coatesville falls short in attempt to knock in their 62–51 quarter-final win over [[Pennridge School District|Pennridge]] before play was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news|url=https://papreplive.com/2020/03/12/durens-defense-helps-roman-catholic-overcome-pennridges-heart-in-state-playoffs/|title=Duren's defense helps Roman Catholic overcome Pennridge's heart in PIAA-6A 2nd round|work=PA Prep Live|first=Andrew|last=Robinson|date=March 12, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} At the end of the year he collected first-team all-league, first-team all-state and MaxPreps Sophomore All-American honors.{{cite news|url=https://www.phillytrib.com/sports/basketball/all-catholic-league-boys-basketball-team-announced/article_9b5abf4c-f5d3-54a9-a5de-be5ac2cc9ef8.html|title=All-Catholic League boy's basketball transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]], who was in the process of joining the independent National Interscholastic Basketball Conference (NIBC) with other elite programs like [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill]], [[Wasatch Academy]] and Sunrise Christian amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-mait-advance-0127-20210127-bgozywat4feqfbbtu5bwigg7hy-story.html|title=No. 1 Montverde basketball hosts 2 weekends of big games|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|first=Buddy|last=Collings|date=January 27, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} Duren was one of only five underclassmen named to the [[Sports Illustrated]] Preseason All-American team.{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jalen-duren-catches-shot-block-shots-montverde|title=Elite 2022 F Jalen Duren Prefers Catching Shots Over Swatting Them|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|first=Jason|last=Jordan|date=February 9, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} In January 2021, Duren had a strong showing competing against high-level talent at the St. James NIBC Invitational in [[Washington, D.C.]],{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jalen-duren-kennedy-chandler-stars-shine-at-st-james-nibc-invitational|title=Jalen Duren, Kennedy Chandler, Felix Okpara and Others Shine news|url=https://247sports.com/college/villanova/Article/The-St-James-NIBC-Invitational-Elite-big-man-Jalen-Duren-talks-shop-No-2-2022-recruiting-159485964/|title=The St. James NIBC Invitational: Elite big man Jalen Duren talks shop|work=[[247Sports]]|date=January 17, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} including a [[SportsCenter]] Top 10 play against [[Wasatch Academy]] where he blocked a shot by catching the ball in mid-air. On March 11, Montverde avenged their only loss of the season by defeating Sunrise Christian 61–57 for the inaugural NIBC championship; Duren finished with 13 points and seven rebounds.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/aFsTcZ4LxEmIZY9nKE7wNw/high-school-basketball--no-1-montverde-academy-defeats-no-3-sunrise-christian-academy-61-57-to-win-inaugural-nibc-championship.htm|title=High school basketball: No. 1 Montverde Academy defeats No. 3 Sunrise Christian Academy 61-57 to win inaugural NIBC championship|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 12, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} He averaged 15.5 points, 10.6 rebounds and 2.4 blocks per game in NIBC conference play, leading the Eagles to a 12–1 league record (20–1 overall).{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/K4zTFklsnE6tRRppzkmMkA/jalen-duren-named-2020-21-maxpreps-florida-high-school-basketball-player-of-the-year.htm|title=Jalen Duren named 2020-21 MaxPreps Florida High School Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 11, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2021}} He was also recognized as the 2020–21 MaxPreps Florida High School Basketball Player of the Year. ===Recruiting=== Duren overtook [[Emoni Bates]] in his junior year as the top prospect in the 2022 recruiting class, surpassing Bates as the number one recruit according to [[ESPN]], [[247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On August 6, 2021, he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2021 class and committed to playing college basketball for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] over offers from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (FL)]], the [[NBA G League]] and the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|Australia NBL]].{{Cite = 4 | rivals overall = 3 | espn overall = 7 | access-date = October 2, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On November 19, 2021, Duren scored 19 points, grabbed 19 rebounds and blocked five shots in a 74–62 win against [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky]].{{cite news |title=Duren leads No. 11 Memphis past Western Kentucky 74-62 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401371916 |access-date=March 1, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 19, 2021}} He was named to the First Team release|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2022/3/8/american-athletic-conference-announces-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=American Athletic Conference Announces Men's Basketball Honors|publisher=[[American Athletic Conference]] |date=March 9, 2022 |access-date=March 9, 2022}} Duren led Memphis to their first [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] appearance since [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014]], leading the Tigers to the round of 32.{{Cite web |last=Munz |first=Jason |title=Memphis basketball pushes Gonzaga to brink but falls short in NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2022/03/19/memphis-basketball-ncaa-tournament-run-ends-loss-gonzaga/7107955001/ |access-date=April 18, 2022 |website=The Commercial Appeal}} As a freshman, he averaged 12 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game. On April 18, 2022, Duren declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=April 18, 2022 |title=Jalen Duren, after developing 'in a lot of different ways' in one season with Memphis men's basketball program, will enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33762796 |access-date=February 17, 2026 |website=ESPN.com|last=Givony|first=Jonathan}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2022–2026) === Duren was selected with the 13th overall pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2022 NBA web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pistons-news-lebron-james-record-matched-by-jalen-duren-after-monster-stat-line|title=LeBron James record matched by Jalen Duren after monster stat line in Pistons vs. blocks in a 122–119 overtime comeback victory over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He also logged his third career 30+/15+ game, the most by any Pistons player before turning 23. Duren became the first Pistons player since [[Bob McAdoo]] in 1980 to record four straight 25+/10+ games, and the youngest in the NBA to do so since [[Luka Dončić]] in 2019–20.{{cite web |title=Starting 5, Feb. 28: Shai's return, OT thrillers for both top seeds & B-day Luka leads Lakers vs. Dubs on ABC |url=https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-feb-28-shais-return-ot-thrillers-for-both-top-seeds-b-day-luka-leads-lakers-vs-dubs-on-abc |website=NBA.com |date=February 28, 2024 |access-date=February 28, 2026}} On May 24, Duren was named to the [[All-NBA]] Third Team, earning the first All-NBA selection of his career.{{cite web |title=2025–26 Kia All-NBA Teams announced |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-all-nba-teams-announced |website=NBA.com |date=2026-05-24 |access-date=2026-05-27}} ==National team career== Duren played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in [[Belém]], Brazil.
